title: Send messages immediately and restore per-thread drafts
what: Typing in any thread gives immediate, truthful delivery feedback and each thread keeps its own unsent draft.
criteria: Enter sends; Shift+Enter inserts a newline; IME composition and skill-menu selection do not accidentally send.
Each thread independently restores its text and attachments after navigation and restart, including legacy draft migration without changing ownership.
Show queued/submitting/accepted/failed or uncertain delivery distinctly; a lost acknowledgement is reconciled without automatic duplicate submission.

Measure local send feedback separately from provider latency; target visible acknowledgement within 100 ms on the agreed Windows fixture and document actual measurements. Preserve disconnected-provider and managed-thread behavior.

title: Organize projects and settle threads or whole projects
what: Navigate project folders containing multiple threads, with recognizable provider icons and reversible Settled groups.
criteria: Create/open projects and create multiple threads under each; retain existing thread IDs, provider bindings, project memory scopes and disconnected-provider history.
Settle a thread and restore it under its owning project. Settle an entire project and restore its thread group without changing individual prior settled states.
Retain search and working/attention indicators. Settling or hiding a view never deletes history, working files, branches or running native work.

An empty unstarted thread may choose any ready provider; a started native conversation stays with its original provider. Same-provider controls respect native capabilities. Verify the existing provider/coordinator separation.

title: Render readable answers and attachment previews
what: Read rich, streaming answers with usable code, tables, links and attachments in the existing Threads view.
criteria: Render Markdown paragraphs, lists, tables, quotes, links and highlighted code with copy controls; preserve streaming partial content and existing history.
Show supported image attachments and useful file/link metadata rather than only filenames; preserve provider-specific attachment limits and explicit unsupported feedback.
Keep user scroll position while reading earlier messages; offer jump-to-latest without forcing scrolling. Long transcripts remain responsive.
Treat message markup as content, not executable UI; inspect real Windows renders and keyboard interactions at desktop and minimum sizes.

title: Render and inspect diagrams in answers
what: Agent-generated Mermaid diagrams render inside answers and can be enlarged and copied.
criteria: Render complete valid diagram blocks; show readable source while incomplete or invalid, with a useful error instead of a blank answer.
Support zoom/focused inspection and copying diagram source; retain accessible text/source and streaming behavior.
Diagram content cannot execute arbitrary scripts or fetch arbitrary resources through the renderer.
Verify representative sequence, flow and state diagrams, malformed input and light/dark presentation as themes become available.

title: Follow Codex tool activity and subagents
what: See Codex's current work and expandable tool results alongside readable answers.
criteria: Add activity records beside existing messages without rewriting historical identities; preserve order and deduplicate replayed native events.
Show available commands, file changes, results, errors, reasoning/status summaries and subagent lifecycle with elapsed time; never invent hidden reasoning or unavailable details.
Persist sufficient activity for reload/reconnect to restore the work log without re-running tools or duplicating the final answer.
Extract the shared activity presentation seam as part of this complete Codex path. Exercise native event fixtures and a bounded installed-client smoke journey.

title: Follow Claude tool activity and subagents
what: Claude threads expose the same useful activity view through Claude's native event stream.
criteria: Map native Claude events to the established activity view, retaining provider-specific details and actual ordering.
Show running/completed/failed commands, file operations and available subagent status with expandable output.
Reconnect/reload restores history and pending state without duplicate tool execution or messages.
Keep the current streaming CLI unless concrete capability evidence warrants the SDK used by T3; compare that decision with the reference and verify an installed-client smoke journey.

title: Follow Grok tool activity and subagents
what: Grok threads expose native ACP work through the shared activity view.
criteria: Map ACP tool and lifecycle updates plus supported native extensions into the existing activity view.
Display available commands, output, file changes, failures and subagents; unavailable fields remain unavailable rather than inferred as facts.
Recover from reconnect and replay without duplicated actions, output or answers.
Verify ACP event fixtures and a bounded installed-client smoke journey against the shared adapter contract.

title: Queue follow-up messages and explicitly steer a running turn
what: Send another message while work is running, with a durable queue and an explicit Steer now action.
criteria: Queue per thread by default; edit/remove items before dispatch and keep order across restart. Maintain separation from the attention queue and uncertain-command outbox.
Dispatch once when the current turn finishes; reconcile interrupted acknowledgements without silently replaying uncertain messages.
Steer now uses the selected provider's supported native mechanism. If unsupported, explain that limitation without silently cancelling or pretending steering succeeded.
Keep other threads usable during slow sends; test concurrent threads, interruption, failures, permissions waiting and managed-to-manual handoff.

title: Answer structured questions and approvals in the right thread
what: Respond to complete native questions and approval requests while keeping their thread and tool context visible.
criteria: Render all native question items, choices and supported free-text answers, not just the first question.
Show command/tool context and the approval choices actually supported by the owning provider; do not invent broader permission grants.
Route each answer to its original pending request even after pane changes or reconnect; resolve once and show failures without losing the request.
Verify Codex, Claude and Grok request fixtures, simultaneous requests in different threads, and keyboard accessibility. Preserve existing policy and assignment authority.

title: Drag a second thread into a split workspace
what: Drag a thread from the sidebar beside the current thread and use both independently.
criteria: Dragging a second thread splits available space evenly; dividers resize and either thread can receive input without draft or selection leakage.
Both views retain their own message position, provider controls and activity; cross-project panes are supported.
Closing a pane closes only its view; the agent keeps working and remains reachable in the sidebar.
Provide a keyboard-accessible way to open/focus/close a split and verify minimum-width behavior. Extract a reusable thread-view boundary only as needed for this slice.

title: Add three- and four-thread layouts and restore the workspace
what: Arrange more threads with the agreed snapping rules and restore the arrangement after restart.
criteria: A third thread spans the row below the first two; a fourth creates a 2-by-2 grid. A single-row arrangement is available with adjustable dividers.
Persist arrangement, selected threads and sizing; reopen existing threads without starting new native work.
Offer focus/zoom for smaller windows and return to the retained layout. One-through-four arrangements are defaults, not an implicit hard cap.
Handle closing, moving and adding panes without losing drafts or live state; verify cross-project layout and recovery at desktop/minimum sizes.

title: Browse files in a shared, pinnable tools panel
what: Open a Files surface beside a thread and inspect files in that thread's actual working directory.
criteria: Provide a reusable side-panel surface selector and file tree with readable text/Markdown/image previews and copyable paths.
Panel follows the focused thread and can be pinned; paths and workspace identity remain visible when focus changes.
Read the thread's bound working directory, including a worktree when present; missing files and unavailable folders produce recoverable states.
Retain panel state across focus changes and integrate with split panes when available. Verify actual Electron file browsing without exposing unrestricted renderer filesystem access.

title: Run a persistent terminal beside a thread
what: Open and use an interactive terminal in the active thread's working directory.
criteria: Launch a real shell/PTY with input, output, resize, interrupt, scrollback and exit state; support multiple terminal instances needed for a dev server and commands.
Keep terminal sessions alive across thread focus and panel hiding; identify the owning directory and respect panel pinning.
On app restart show the true terminal lifecycle rather than claiming a dead process resumed; support a clear reopen action.
Verify on the target Windows desktop, including a running dev server and shell interruption, and preserve platform-appropriate launch behavior.

title: Browse inside Sotto and choose where links open
what: Use the embedded browser for local apps and URLs while ordinary agent links open externally by default.
criteria: Default normal web-link clicks to the user's system browser; persist a setting to use the in-app browser instead and expose either destination per link.
Embedded browser supports navigation, back/forward, reload, URL display and multiple retained pages needed for daily work.
Keep page state across panel focus/pinning; clearly identify the browser destination and handle unavailable local servers.
Use the desktop browser security boundary so visited pages do not inherit Sotto's privileged application bridge. Verify an actual local app and an external link.

title: Create independent thread worktrees
what: New independent coding tasks get their own working copy and branch, with an explicit shared-working-copy option.
criteria: Create/reuse a Git worktree during thread creation and bind all provider commands to the actual working directory.
Offer a deliberate shared-working-copy path for collaborating threads; existing threads remain in their current folders and non-Git folders remain usable.
Worktree setup failure leaves a recoverable thread draft and never routes a task into the wrong directory; preserve project-level memory scope across worktrees.
Verify concurrent native threads do not overwrite each other's working files. Include worktree status/open/reveal behavior and preserve user changes during cleanup.

title: Review Git changes in the selected thread
what: Inspect current working changes and diffs from the thread's own branch and worktree.
criteria: Show changed, new and deleted files with readable diffs and selection that follows the focused or pinned thread.
Refresh when tools or terminal commands change files, without overwriting the user's reading position or showing another thread's worktree.
Support large/binary/unavailable files with explicit fallback and copy/open actions.
Verify two threads with different worktrees and a shared-working-copy case; this slice must be useful before commit and PR controls land.

title: Stage, commit and manage the active branch
what: Complete local Git work from Sotto using the selected thread's working copy.
criteria: Show staged versus unstaged changes, allow deliberate staging/unstaging and create a commit with an editable message.
Expose current branch and appropriate checkout/create-branch controls; preserve dirty changes and report conflicts or detached state accurately.
Refresh the diff and branch state after actions; a failed action remains actionable and never reports success early.
Verify normal commit, empty commit prevention, dirty branch switching and separate worktree isolation using temporary repositories.

title: Push work and open the pull-request surface
what: Push a branch, create/open its pull request and follow review/check status inside Sotto.
criteria: Use the configured repository identity and existing authentication; show target remote/base branch and editable PR title/body before the user's action.
Create or open the existing PR without duplicates; display actual review and check status with refresh and useful authentication/network errors.
Open relevant PR links according to browser preference and associate the surface with the correct branch/worktree.
Verify against a controlled repository or faithful API fixtures plus an authorized end-to-end smoke action; do not silently merge or publish merely from viewing a thread.

title: Inspect checkpoints and perform supported thread reverts
what: Review changes associated with completed work and explicitly revert when the native provider supports matching conversation rollback.
criteria: Record/recover checkpoint associations without changing thread/provider identities; display the affected file changes before acting.
Coordinate working-file restoration with native conversation rollback, with clear confirmation of what will change.
Respect provider capability differences, including Grok's lack of native rollback in the pinned reference; never present a file-only change as a complete conversation rewind.
Guard active/pending work and preserve unrelated edits; verify interrupted revert recovery and unsupported-provider states.

title: Browse and invoke Codex skills
what: Type / or $ to find and select Codex's available personal and project skills.
criteria: Discover enabled, user-invocable skills for the selected Codex account and actual working directory; preserve native names, descriptions and scope precedence.
Search and select through the composer; selection inserts a skill invocation for review rather than immediately starting work.
Refresh changed catalogs and distinguish native commands from skills; preserve normal manual native syntax and keyboard send behavior.
Verify native invocation and catalog failures. Build the shared picker/capability seam within this complete Codex slice; no skill editing or installation UI.

title: Browse and invoke Claude skills
what: Use the same picker for Claude's own global and project skills.
criteria: Discover from Claude's configured native sources and honor enabled/invocable flags and duplicate-name precedence.
Translate the selected invocation as required by Claude, including multi-mention limitations, rather than assuming Codex syntax works unchanged.
Show only the selected provider's relevant catalog, including skills found in the thread's worktree scope.
Verify selected and manually typed invocation with native fixtures and an installed-client smoke journey; no skill management UI.

title: Browse and invoke Grok skills
what: Use the shared picker for the skills Grok actually exposes and can invoke.
criteria: Discover native personal/project/plugin skills through Grok's supported catalog interface, honoring invocation availability.
Send native invocations through ACP and verify real expansion rather than treating text transport as proof of skill use.
Refresh account/directory changes and show unavailable discovery or invocation honestly.
Cover catalog errors, multiple mentions and reconnect in fixtures plus an installed-client smoke journey; no new Sotto skill engine.

title: Show live tokens, context and estimated thread cost
what: Read compact native usage indicators while working without opening a separate analytics dashboard.
criteria: Display provider-reported token activity and current context usage near the composer, with elapsed time where available.
Accumulate supported usage into a clearly labeled estimated thread cost using versioned rate inputs; distinguish an API-equivalent estimate from actual subscription billing.
Handle missing fields, caching, provider resets and model changes without inventing counts, double-counting replayed events or presenting unavailable data as zero.
Verify known usage fixtures and compare installed-client observations; detailed usage reports remain outside scope.

title: Match T3's native compaction behavior
what: Use the provider's normal compaction strategy and T3's context recommendation and controls.
criteria: Offer native manual compaction only where supported, prevent duplicate in-flight requests and report actual completion/failure.
Match the pinned proactive Claude predicate: at least 100,000 context tokens and at least 70 minutes since the last context update; suppress during running/pending states as T3 does.
Match Keep full history dismissal per context snapshot and native Claude resume-return choices, including Don't ask again; do not claim the heuristic measures cache expiry.
Preserve native auto-compaction defaults and explicit overrides; verify clock-controlled boundary cases and Codex/Claude/Grok capability differences without a custom summarizer.

title: Start and resume a project-free Sotto chat with Codex
what: Open the Sotto area, start a saved conversation without a project and talk to the configured Codex coordinator with its normal skills.
criteria: Add durable personal-chat identity and history without inventing a fake user project or rebinding existing project threads; record the additive terminology/persistence decision.
Offer New chat and saved chats, preserving each native conversation and the rule that a started conversation stays with its provider.

Use normal native Codex skills and conversation behavior, not the constrained command parser. Retrieve relevant existing global memory without granting new authority or leaking project-private context.
Verify restart, provider disconnect, changed coordinator defaults for new chats and coexistence with explicit project-thread management. No automatic project creation or delegation.

title: Use Claude for persistent Sotto chats
what: Start project-free Sotto conversations with the configured Claude coordinator and resume them later.
criteria: Use Claude's native persistent conversation path with normal available skills, not the tool-disabled ephemeral classification path.
Reuse saved-chat navigation, scoped memory and rich answer rendering while retaining provider-specific history and permissions.
Changing the configured coordinator affects new chats and leaves existing Codex/Claude bindings intact.
Verify native create/send/resume, restart, skills and errors, without introducing a separate workflow harness.

title: Use Grok for persistent Sotto chats
what: Start and resume project-free Sotto conversations with Grok and its normal native skills.
criteria: Use a durable native Grok conversation with its available skills and preserve ACP pending requests/history.
Reuse saved-chat navigation, scoped memory and rich rendering; coordinator changes do not move existing chats across providers.
Preserve project-thread management and global versus project memory boundaries.
Verify native create/send/resume, restart, skill invocation and connection failure without automatic project work.

title: Talk and dictate in the active Sotto conversation
what: Type, dictate or have a spoken exchange in the selected personal Sotto chat.
criteria: Route existing MAI dictation into the focused personal chat and allow review/editing; conversational voice turns and replies append to that same saved history.
Use the established Grok voice default and Kokoro option, with interruption/mute and clear listening/speaking state.
Prevent speech from being routed to a different chat after focus changes or interpreted as an implicit authorization to create/manage project work.
Verify all three coordinator providers and a physical microphone-to-response journey on Windows; report measured latency honestly and retain the existing voice-budget issue's unresolved limits.

title: Turn a brainstorming chat into an editable prompt
what: Generate a useful prompt from a Sotto conversation for the user to copy and use themselves.
criteria: Produce objective, relevant decisions/context, constraints/non-goals, deliverables, acceptance checks and unresolved questions, omitting empty sections.
Honor the latest corrections and separate accepted decisions from suggestions; do not invent missing requirements or silently resolve contradictions.
Show editable/copyable output and preserve the original chat. The action never creates a project, starts a thread or delegates work.

Evaluate a representative fixture set of short/long brainstorming, changed decisions and missing details against a documented fidelity/usefulness rubric, including human review before declaring the format proven.

title: Choose light, dark or system appearance and an accent
what: Configure Sotto's appearance while retaining its typography, identity and readable native controls.
criteria: Add persisted light/dark/system and accent choices with immediate preview and correct initial/migrated settings.
Apply themes across existing rooms, settings, provider controls and shared Threads surfaces; new feature slices must honor the same tokens.
Supersede the prior black-only product requirement explicitly while preserving dictation behavior and the floating widget's separate behavior unless technically required.
Visually verify contrast, focus, native dropdowns, motion preferences and scale coverage; evolve the capture matrix rather than deleting quality gates.

title: Verify the complete daily workspace and recovery journey
what: Demonstrate the complete agreed daily workflow with mixed providers, working tools and recoverable state.
criteria: Using the agreed native foundation, open/create a project, run independent threads, inspect activity/diagrams, use terminal/browser/files, review changes, commit and open a PR; also exercise personal chat, voice, skills and prompt generation.
Verify pane pinning/focus, theme/browser preferences, thread/project settle/restore, unsent drafts, queued messages and reconnect/restart recovery without cross-thread actions or duplicate sends.

Measure local send feedback, stream rendering and pane responsiveness separately from provider/network latency on representative long histories; fix material regressions and retain explicit unsupported-provider states.

Inspect actual Windows desktop/minimum-size layouts and repeat important journeys on supported macOS before calling them cross-platform verified. Confirm final behavior against the user references; native delivery under existing #24 is a release gate.
